driver: issue #43 (description compression to the amended §3.5 listing-budget target)
method: HOUSECARL_SKILL_AUTHORING §6.5 fan-out, menu variant per houseCARL PR #295: one fresh-context judge per eval query (Opus, HIGH reasoning effort, no tools), each shown ONLY its single query plus the full lettered menu of all 11 NEW descriptions (anonymized, under-test skill unflagged) plus NONE, forced single pick, reasoning before verdict; one Opus adjudicator per skill scored recall/specificity from the judges' reasoning per §6.5 step 4. Judge model deliberately upgraded from PR #295's sonnet-low (maintainer decision). Contamination guard: the live install was moved aside for the fan-out window so fresh judges carried no stale skill listing. Gates: recall >= 80%, specificity >= 50%. Scope limit of this measurement: judges saw the clean, full-text 11-entry menu, so the fan-out validates discriminability among the 11 descriptions - NOT routing survival under the listing-truncation pressure issue #43 describes; the post-merge /doctor budget check is the separate, remaining test of that.
description_measured: Patch an NPC, enemy, follower, or boss for Requiem via houseCARL — the whole actor: fixed level, class, combat style, factions, perks, and racial trait inheritance derived from Requiem's comparable actor into an ESP override. Use for any NPC_ record: a boss dying to one arrow, an enemy too strong or weak, a follower to integrate, creature actors whose unrecognized race leaves them missing Requiem's traits. Load before the NPC_ write.
adjudicator_notes: No overrides applied — every judge's reasoning matched its verdict token, including q4 (reasoning explicitly argues for I and picks I). Note the F/I boundary is the only contested surface: q4 (miss) and q9 (hit) are the same collision — unclassified creature race vs. the actors on it — decided only by whether the user names the actors as the target ("fix the NPCs" → F) or names race-level symptoms ("takes wrong damage, missing traits" → I). Both descriptions claim the phrase "missing Requiem traits", so the split is coin-flippy rather than principled; a disambiguating clause in F (e.g. defer to RACE when the only symptoms are racial damage/traits and no actor field is wrong) or a matching pointer in I would harden it. No specificity pressure at all — F was named as a considered-and-rejected near neighbour in 6 of 9 expect=false rows (q10, q11, q12, q14, q15, q17, q18) and correctly rejected each time, so the description is not over-broad; the only cost is recall on the race boundary.
